key_insight: A 4-qubit VQC can detect cyberattacks on NSL-KDD with 88% accuracy, but its performance appears capped by data compression and limited quantum-state expressiveness rather than optimizer failure.
engineering_relevance: For near-term quantum ML in cybersecurity, the main design challenge is choosing an encoding and model size that preserve separability while remaining feasible on NISQ hardware.
method: 4-qubit variational quantum classifier with a 24-parameter trainable ansatz
Amplitude encoding of 16 principal components from the NSL-KDD 20% subset
Compared COBYLA vs SPSA and benchmarked against a tiny classical MLP
evidence_signal: On a held-out binary test split, the VQC reached a stable 88% accuracy, while a class-balanced 22-class in-sample probe collapsed to 9% accuracy.
watch_item: The results do not fully disentangle the effects of encoding, ansatz depth, optimizer budget, and measurement decoding, so the observed limits may not be purely due to the quantum model itself.
paper_title: Evaluation of Variational Quantum Classifiers (VQC) for Cyberattack Detection in the NISQ Era
